Send clicks on a chart to shiny

Source: R/clickevents.R
rvisClickEvents.Rd

Adds javascript to an htmlwidget so that a click on one of its items (a node or link of a graph, a point, bar or slice of a chart) sets a shiny input. The javascript is added with htmlwidgets::onRender() and runs after the widget is drawn: the javascript of the plotting package is not copied or changed, so later versions of the package keep working.

Usage

rvisClickEvents(widget, inputId = NULL, selector = NULL, ids = NULL)

Arguments

widget

An htmlwidget, for example a chart returned by rvisPlot() (rAmCharts charts, which are not htmlwidgets until they are plotted, are converted).

inputId

Name of the shiny input. If NULL, the id of the output followed by _item_click (some widgets, like DiagrammeR and billboarder charts, set their own input <outputId>_click).

selector

CSS selector of the clickable elements, for widgets which are not supported directly.

ids

Optional named vector: ids reported instead of the ids found in the widget (names), for example the keys of graph nodes whose diagram uses internal node numbers. Charts made by rvis (like grviz graphs) keep these ids themselves.

Value

The widget, with the click javascript added.

Details

In shiny, the input is input$<outputId>_item_click (or input[[inputId]] if inputId is given). Its value is a list with field type ("node", "link", "point" or "element") and, as available, id, label, series, index, value, x, y, source and target (links), group and data. It is set again on every click, also when the same item is clicked twice.

Supported widgets: Graphviz diagrams (DiagrammeR::grViz() and the grviz charts of rvis), networkD3 networks, echarts4r, apexcharter, plotly, highcharter, rAmCharts, c3, billboarder, visNetwork, dygraphs and leaflet charts, DT tables (clicks on cells: type "cell", with row, column and value) and rvis coffeewheel sunbursts (type "node", with depth and parent). Leaflet markers and shapes (type "marker" or "shape") report their layerId as id, their group and the clicked lat and lng. For any other widget, give a CSS selector of its clickable elements: the input then gets the element's id (its data-id attribute, svg title or id), its text and its d3 data, if any.

Outside shiny, each click also fires the javascript event rvis:click on the widget element.

In a dashboard, give an output item the field click.events: true to add this to the chart returned by its service.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(shiny)
ui = fluidPage(DiagrammeR::grVizOutput("g"), verbatimTextOutput("clicked"))
server = function(input, output){
  output$g = DiagrammeR::renderGrViz(
    rvisClickEvents(DiagrammeR::grViz("digraph {a -> b; b -> c}")))
  output$clicked = renderPrint(str(input$g_item_click))
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
} # }
